ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, officers, signatories, and beneficial owners of any entity shareholder against: HM Treasury Consolidated Sanctions List, United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, Gibraltar Financial Intelligence Unit domestic PEP/risk indicators, and retained EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions Database applicable in Gibraltar. Enhanced due diligence applies on detection of PEP status, adverse media, negative jurisdiction risk, or unusual source-of-wealth indicators. Each screening result must be dated, evidenced, and assigned a risk rating in accordance with the current Gibraltar AML/CFT Guidance Notes.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Gibraltar Companies Registry – official web portal: https://www.gibraltarcompaniesregistry.gi; name reservation is submitted through the electronic Companies Registry e-services platform.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: English is the statutory corporate language. All registered company names must be in Latin script and, for limited-liability entities, must end in 'Limited' or 'Ltd.'. Foreign-script commercial branding may be used as a trade mark but cannot form the registered statutory name. Non-English names must be transliterated into English and must be distinguishably different from existing names in the Gibraltar register.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Banker, Banking, Building Society, Credit Union, Assurance, Insurance, Reinsurance, Trust, Trustee (require prior Gibraltar Financial Services Commission consent)
Royal, Crown, His Majesty, Her Majesty, Prince, Princess, Duke, Duchess, Governor, Government, Minister, Ministry (require Governor/Government approval)
Gibraltar, City of Gibraltar, Chamber of Commerce (require specific institutional consent or statutory authorization)
United Nations, UN, Commonwealth, Red Cross, Red Crescent, Olympic (restricted by protected emblems legislation)
Bermuda, Exempted, Exempt (where use would misleadingly imply a status not granted by the relevant Bermuda Registrar)
Public Limited Company, P.L.C., LLP (restricted statutory suffixes subject to strict eligibility)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation may be extended once for a further period by written request to the Gibraltar Companies Registry before expiry, with payment of the prescribed extension fee. On rejection, the Registrar issues a written refusal notice stating the statutory basis. The applicant may submit written representations to the Registrar within 21 days requesting reconsideration. If the Registrar affirms the refusal, the applicant may appeal to the Supreme Court of Gibraltar by originating application within 21 days of the final determination. Parallel alternative name filings should be made to avoid delaying incorporation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office maintained by a licensed corporate services provider is permissible for this low-risk digital streaming/production entity as a registered-office address and service-of-process point, provided the provider operates a physical office in Bermuda and, if a Gibraltar establishment is created, in Gibraltar. However, a virtual office alone will not satisfy economic-substance expectations for activity-based income, and the entity must retain locally controlled books, records, governance minutes and, where appropriate, resident management substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: approximately 5% per annum for a standard low-risk AML-tier entity with accurate filings and timely UBO updates. The risk rises to approximately 10–15% per annum if the entity is classified as economically substantive under Bermuda or Gibraltar substance rules, elects to maintain no local staff, or exhibits unusual payment flows from app-store and payment-rail channels without sufficient supporting commercial contracts.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Bermuda (home): Government of Bermuda, Ministry of Finance — Office of the Registrar of Companies (no general income-tax registry because Bermuda levies no corporate income tax). Gibraltar (operating jurisdiction): HM Government of Gibraltar — Income Tax Office, Customs and Income Tax Department, Commissioner of Income Tax; official e-portal: Gibraltar Income Tax e-Services (TaxDirect) via gibraltar.gov.gi.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Bermuda Exempted Company (Bermuda Exempted Co) carrying on vertical micro-drama streaming distribution through Gibraltar must: (1) be incorporated in Bermuda as an exempted company, obtaining a Certificate of Exemption and company registration number from the Bermuda Registrar of Companies, and file annual government fee and economic substance declarations (Bermuda does not issue a VAT/TIN because it has no income tax; the new Bermuda corporate income tax at 15% under OECD Pillar Two applies only to multinational groups with EU 750-million consolidated revenue, which the micro-drama vertical does not reach); (2) if commercially established in Gibraltar, register as an overseas company with the Gibraltar Registrar of Companies under the Companies Act (file certified Bermuda incorporation/charter documents, registered office details, director and shareholder registers, local address and representative, and pay registration fees); (3) apply to the Gibraltar Income Tax Office for a Tax Identification Number (TIN / GI number) using the prescribed non-resident company registration form, providing certification of the Bermuda certificate, memorandum and articles, proof of appointment of a local agent/tax representative, and declaration of intended Gibraltar-source activities; (4) register for Gibraltar PAYE and social insurance if staff are engaged and for import-duty accounts if physical goods are imported; no VAT registration is possible or required in Gibraltar because the jurisdiction is outside the UK/EU VAT territory.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Available elections and safeguards include: (i) Bermuda statutory tax protection election evidenced by a Certificate of Exemption under the Exempted Undertakings Tax Protection Act 1966, guaranteeing exemption from Bermuda income/capital-gains tax on streaming revenue until 2035 (subject to substance and fee compliance); (ii) US federal check-the-box election on IRS Form 8832 to treat the Bermuda Exempted Co as either a corporation or a disregarded entity for US tax purposes (default class for a limited-liability foreign eligible entity is a corporation); (iii) Gibraltar territorial-source election — as a non-resident company, chargeability is confined to profits accruing in or derived from Gibraltar, so foreign streaming revenue may be excluded upon contemporaneous documentation; (iv) where treaty or UK/EU VAT obligations arise, no Gibraltar VAT election exists (no VAT system), but a non-established supplier may elect to register under UK VAT OSS or EU non-union OSS to account for VAT on B2C digital services; and (v) hybrid mismatch elections (fiscal-transparent or deemed-PE elections) may be filed under OECD BEPS Action 2 if the entity is treated as transparent in any counterparty state.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No VAT or GST in Gibraltar; Gibraltar is outside the UK and EU VAT territories. The only indirect taxes are selective import customs duties and excise on physical goods. Vertically distributed digital micro-drama streaming subscriptions are outside the scope of Gibraltar indirect tax.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable — Gibraltar has no VAT/GST, so there is no Gibraltar registration threshold or local-currency turnover trigger. For connected inbound markets: UK VAT registration may be required for a non-established supplier selling digital services to UK consumers (no statutory GBP 90,000 threshold applies to non-established suppliers; the GBP 90,000 threshold refers to UK-established taxable persons); EU non-union OSS registration is required for B2C electronic services to EU consumers (the EUR 10,000 per-calendar-year threshold applies only to EU-established suppliers, not to this Bermuda/Gibraltar entity); no threshold applies in the US given the use of app-store distribution with sales/use tax administered by marketplace facilitators.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, or digital stamping mandate exists in Gibraltar. The Income Tax Office operates no e-invoicing clearance platform; invoicing and records must satisfy general record-keeping rules under the Income Tax Act (supplier name/address/TIN, customer, description, consideration, date). For verification, Apple App Store Connect, Google Play Console, and Stripe settlement/customer transaction reports constitute the primary audit trail. If the entity separately registers for UK VAT, HMRC Making Tax Digital requires functional-compatible software and digital links for VAT returns, but not real-time clearance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating claims are structurally not applicable in Gibraltar because Gibraltar imposes no VAT/GST and Bermuda imposes no VAT or income tax on the exempted company. Streaming subscriptions to vertical micro-dramas are electronically supplied services; any UK VAT exposure (if the entity registers as a non-established supplier) arises at the customer's place of supply (UK standard rate 20%), and the services cannot be zero-rated merely because the distributor is offshore. For physical goods only, export zero-rating under VATA 1994 and Gibraltar customs practices is available if goods are removed from the UK/Gibraltar and evidence of export is retained within prescribed time limits.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (only for physical goods shipped from Gibraltar or the UK; not required for digital micro-drama downloads)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill (proof of physical removal where zero-rating of goods is claimed)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank/FX settlement statement evidencing repatriation of platform revenues within 180 days
App store settlement reports (Apple, Google Play, Stripe) evidencing location of global end-consumers and gross streaming consideration
Bermuda Certificate of Exemption and Gibraltar economic substance filing, confirming tax-exempt status and territorial sourcing
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent export zero-rating claims or artificial diversion of streaming income attract criminal and civil sanctions in both applicable territories: in Bermuda, false declarations under the Exempted Companies Act void the exemption certificate and may trigger company strike-off, fines, and reimposition of hypothetical Bermuda tax; in Gibraltar, the Income Tax Office may recharacterise offshore receipts as Gibraltar-source on management-and-control, permanent-establishment, or anti-avoidance grounds, make transfer-pricing adjustments, and impose penalties of up to 100% of under-assessed tax plus interest, with criminal prosecution for deliberate evasion; in the UK, any fraudulent VAT zero-rating claim on connected supplies is clawed back by HMRC with up to 100% penalty under VATA 1994 sections 60 and 67, in addition to interest and retrospective assessment of 20% output VAT; economic substance non-compliance in Bermuda or Gibraltar can independently trigger deregistration and dissolution.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of England (monetary authority for the Gibraltar Pound under the Currency Notes Act 1934 as applied to Gibraltar, regulating issuance and redemption at fixed 1:1 parity with GBP); HM Government of Gibraltar (sole issuer of GIP banknotes and coins); Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) as prudential supervisor and competent authority for Gibraltar-licensed banks under the Financial Services Act 2019 (Gibraltar). For Bermuda-headquartered treasury activities, the Bermuda Monetary Authority (BMA) administers exchange-control permissions only for Bermuda-dollar transactions and imposes no restriction on free use of USD/GBP/EUR in external accounts.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: GIP is fully convertible into GBP at a fixed 1:1 parity and, through GBP, is freely convertible into USD, EUR, and CNH without exchange-control approval. The UK/Gibraltar combined regime applies no current-account or capital-account restrictions, permitting unfettered profit repatriation, dividend declarations, IP royalty payments, intercompany loan repayments, and shareholder distributions from the Gibraltar branch to the Bermuda parent and onward to non-resident shareholders. No Gibraltar withholding tax applies to outbound dividends, interest, royalties, or rental payments made by a Gibraltar-resident company to non-resident payees, and the Bermuda exempted company benefits from a zero corporate tax rate in Bermuda subject to Economic Substance Act 2018 filing obligations. The only frictions are documentary: banks will require CRS/FATCA self-certifications (Form W-8BEN-E and CRS tax-residency declarations) and a commercially rational explanation of the Bermuda entity's role as the IP/financing holding vehicle to prevent re-characterisation of the structure as tax evasion or aggressive avoidance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory timelines and no mandatory conversion ratios for export proceeds in either Gibraltar or Bermuda. A Gibraltar-resident branch or merchant subsidiary may retain 100% of foreign-currency export earnings (USD, EUR, CNH) in non-GIP bank accounts, may convert any amount to GIP/GBP at the fixed 1:1 parity, and may deploy proceeds offshore without a domestic foreign-exchange market settlement requirement. Bermuda likewise imposes no surrender rules on USD receipts of an exempted company, provided the BMA receives statistical notification where Bermuda-dollar currency is involved. This enables the treasury to retain USD revenue for production and acquisition costs without forced conversion losses.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: 2/5 for the Bermuda exempted company alone; 4/5 for a Gibraltar-registered branch or subsidiary. Legal constraints: (i) Apple In-App Purchase, Google Play Billing, and Stripe require payout to a real bank account in the merchant-company's country of registration or tax nexus; virtual IBANs issued by fintech EMIs are not accepted by Apple or Google treasury operations; (ii) UK-authorised EMIs (Wise, Airwallex, Currenxie, MultiPass) generally decline pure Bermuda exempted companies lacking a UK Companies House overseas-company branch registration, a UK VAT registration, or a CRS/FATCA category acceptable to their acquiring banks; (iii) EMIs remain feasible only for operational disbursements below USD 250,000 per month (cloud hosting, programmatic ad buying, distributed cast and creator payroll) and must be capped as concentration-risk counterparties in the treasury policy; (iv) Card-acquiring EMI rails cannot be used to settle Apple/Google trade funds due to platform-imposed settlement restrictions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical attendance at a Gibraltar bank's head office is not an absolute statutory mandate for low-risk corporate accounts. All five licensed banks accept a fully remote opening if the Bermuda entity provides: (a) a board resolution authorising account opening and named signatories; (b) notarised and Hague Apostilled corporate documents from the Bermuda Registrar of Companies; (c) a real-time video compliance interview with the UBO or a delegated director incorporating digital ID verification and liveness detection; and (d) a bankers' reference from the shareholder's existing bank in Hong Kong or Singapore. In practice, 100% remote onboarding is achievable where a Gibraltar-licensed TCSP (trust and company service provider) acts as introducer and maintains the registered-office and record-keeping obligation; otherwise the bank mandates the UBO or one director to attend an in-person interview in Gibraltar or at a London office of First Bank, Gibraltar International Bank, or Banco Sabadell. The interview covers source of wealth, source of funds, the corporate organogram, and the revenue logic of the Apple/Google app-store flow.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bermuda exempted company claiming tax-exempt status without verifiable economic substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bermuda Registrar Certificate of Good Standing; annual Bermuda Economic Substance (International Business Companies) Act 2018 filing and declaration showing the entity conducts financing and IP-holding activities; audited financial statements of the Bermuda parent; Gibraltar TCSP substance letter confirming the registered office, branch records, and bookkeeping location; written confirmation that operating profits are taxed in Gibraltar at 12.5% to remove tax-evasion red flags.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume inbound credits from Apple (Ireland/United States) and Google (Ireland/Singapore) without visible commercial contracts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed Apple Developer Program Licence Agreement, Apple Paid Applications Schedule, Google Play Developer Distribution Agreement, and Stripe Merchant Agreement; App Store Connect and Google Play Console screenshots showing the merchant legal-entity name; historical and projected monthly payout reports from the platforms; narrative treasury flow from platform payouts to production costs; confirmation that the merchant of record is the enrolled entity in the developer programme.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO source of funds arriving from Hong Kong/Singapore holding structures with opaque intermediary layers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passports and utility bills of all natural persons owning 25% or more; certified incorporation and good-standing certificates of UBO holding companies; independent banker's reference from the UBO's principal bank in Hong Kong or Singapore; formal source-of-wealth statement (net worth schedule, employment history, prior exits); trust deed if the UBO is held through a discretionary trust; six months of bank statements evidencing the capital injection trail and consistency with declared wealth.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tethered production disbursements to China-based micro-drama studios without international invoice standards
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed short-drama production licensing and services agreements (Chinese original with notarised English translation); studio business license and beneficial-owner declarations; itemised production budgets with milestone schedules; clearance certificates from the Chinese customs/SAFE administration where cross-border remittance requires them; group procurement policy; advance-payment structure capped at 30% of the production budget and supported by milestone certificates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unregulated entertainment streaming business resembling gambling, premium-rate fraud, or high-chargeback typologies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: GFSC written confirmation that no financial-services licence is required for a video-on-demand operator; content-chain-of-title and copyright register evidencing ownership of the micro-drama library; Apple and Google consumer refund policies and chargeback-control statistics; data-protection and GDPR compliance documentation under the Gibraltar Data Protection Act 2004; evidence that IAP receipts are settled net of platform commissions in accordance with Apple/Google terms to demonstrate expected treasury volumes.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The initial USD 50,000–100,000 shareholder injection (equity or subordinated shareholder loan) is routed from the UBO's Hong Kong or Singapore account to the Gibraltar bank's USD correspondent (typically Bank of New York Mellon, JPMorgan Chase, or Citibank New York) via SWIFT MT103. Field 70/Remittance Information must state 'CAPITAL INJECTION - BERMUDA EXEMPTED CO - GIBRALTAR BRANCH' and be accompanied by the board resolution for capital increase, the Bermuda Director's Certificate, the Bermuda share allotment form, and source-of-funds bank statements. No Gibraltar exchange-control approval is required, but the receiving bank must file a currency-transaction report to the GFSC for deposits above EUR 10,000, and the Gibraltar branch must file its Annual Return under the Gibraltar Companies Act 2014 if registered as a branch of an overseas company; the proceeds may be held in the USD Capital Escrow Account until the bank confirms the commercial purpose and CRS/FATCA classification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Production and distribution payments settle via (i) SWIFT MT103 for USD/GBP supplier payments above GBP 3,000; (ii) SEPA Instant or SEPA Credit Transfer for EU-based post-production houses using IBANs; (iii) UK Faster Payments or CHAPS for UK advertising agencies and staff payroll; (iv) Commercial Letters of Credit under ICC UCP600 for China-studio production commitments above USD 250,000, opened by the Gibraltar bank for the Bermuda parent with the studio's confirming bank (e.g. Bank of China, Hong Kong branch) receiving MT700; and (v) Hong Kong CHATS and the Offshore RMB clearing system (CNH) for settlements with contracted Hong Kong distribution partners. Because Apple IAP, Google Play Billing, and Stripe pay only to a bank account in the merchant country, a UK-registered overseas-company branch (Companies House Part 34) must maintain a GBP/USD settlement account at a UK clearing bank (e.g. Barclays UK, HSBC UK, or Mettle/Lighthouse EMI for volumes below USD 100,000) to receive the payout wires; the Gibraltar bank then consolidates balances nightly for FX conversion and investment. All outbound payments must carry a valid purpose code (e.g. ROY for royalties, LIC for licences, PUR for production) and pass the bank's sanctions screening against OFAC, UK OPSI, and consolidated EU lists.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forward contracts (USD/GBP, USD/EUR, USD/CNH) with tenors up to 12 months offered by Gibraltar-licensed credit institutions
Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on USD/CNY executed with an authorised NDF market-maker in Hong Kong or London to hedge legacy renminbi exposure on China studio disbursements
FX swaps (USD/GBP, EUR/GBP) for rolling operating liquidity without creating open currency positions
Cross-currency swaps (USD/CNH, USD/GBP) for matched funding of production loans or commercial-letter-of-credit exposure
Vanilla FX call and put options (EUR/USD, USD/CNH) purchased from tier-1 bank counterparties to cap adverse currency movement without margin-call exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment surcharge of 5% per month (max 50%); persistent default triggers administrative strike-off and prohibition on carrying on business.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Gibraltar Registrar of Companies (Companies House Gibraltar)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after each anniversary of registration in Gibraltar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty escalates from GIP 60 to GIP 300 per default; continued default gives grounds for compulsory strike-off and director disqualification.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) / Beneficial Ownership Registrar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Simultaneously with the Confirmation Statement; within 42 days after anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to GIP 5,000 and daily default fines; breach is a criminal offence and may restrict banking relationships.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 30 November following the calendar tax year (or approved fiscal year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Tax-geared penalty up to 100%; statutory interest at 3% above central bank rate; enforcement through distraint and court proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 6 months after the end of the financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fixed penalty up to USD 10,000; daily default fine up to USD 1,000; potential imprisonment of officers for deliberate non-compliance; information exchange with EU authorities.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Bermuda: mandatory audit if a company exceeds USD 10M in assets, USD 20M in turnover, or is a public company; shareholders holding 10% may demand an audit. Gibraltar overseas company branch: audit required if parent carrying on business through branch and both turnover > GIP 8.4M and balance sheet > GIP 4.2M, or > 50 employees; otherwise no filing of audited accounts required for small branches.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (Gibraltar Companies Act 2014 requires a true and fair view under IFRS; Bermuda permits IFRS, US GAAP, or Canadian GAAP for exempted companies).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Gibraltar corporate secretary must obtain and verify UBO declarations annually; any change in ownership of more than 25% must be filed within 30 days. The company must submit a UBO confirmation to the Gibraltar Beneficial Ownership Registrar simultaneously with the Confirmation Statement.
